source.title: Dynamical origin for winner-take-all competition in a biological network of the hippocampal dentate gyrus

confidence_rationale: This is the most directly IMPLEMENTABLE reference in the pull: it is a spiking-network model that states the winner-take-all selection rule as an explicit, reproducible mechanism (per-cluster feedback inhibition, with survival determined by whether a unit's time-averaged excitatory:inhibitory conductance ratio exceeds a threshold), rather than describing WTA qualitatively. That makes it useful as a specification for the H3 operator in a way the electrophysiology papers are not. Confidence is held at 0.66 rather than higher for two independent reasons. First, source quality: Physical Review E is a solid physics venue but this is a modelling paper with no new empirical data, and it inherits rather than tests the WTA premise -- it explains HOW WTA arises given an assumed circuit, it does not establish THAT the dentate gyrus does WTA. Second, mapping fidelity: the model's competition is organised into lamellar clusters each with one basket cell, and the mechanism depends on conductance-based spiking dynamics with a meaningful time axis, none of which has a counterpart in SD-016's single-tick feedforward tagger over 16 slots. The value here is the ALGORITHMIC SKELETON (relative-drive competition against a shared inhibitory pool, thresholded, yielding sparse survival), which transfers; the biophysics does not.
failure_signatures: The WTA outcome in this model depends on a THRESHOLD on the E-I conductance ratio: units above R_th survive, all others go silent. A selection mechanism implemented with a soft/graded competition term but no effective thresholding non-linearity may reproduce the uniform-mixing outcome rather than sparse selection -- which is precisely the SD-016 418d/e/i failure signature (an auxiliary diversification loss on a plain softmax achieved population-level diversity without breaking the entropy ceiling).

Competition is LOCAL to a lamellar cluster (one basket cell per cluster), not global across the whole granule-cell population. A single global inhibition/normalisation term over all 16 SD-016 slots is a different architecture from the modelled one, and the paper gives no reason to expect it behaves equivalently.

The model reports that mossy-cell death and adult-born immature granule cells both perturb the WTA competition -- i.e. the sparse-selection regime is sensitive to the composition of the competing population, not robust to it. An REE slot array whose slots have heterogeneous or drifting effective gain may not sit in the WTA regime at all.
Sparsity in the model is ~5% activation of granule cells. Scaled to 16 slots this is below one slot, so the modelled operating regime does not straightforwardly instantiate at SD-016's slot count.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a conductance-based spiking model of the dentate gyrus, granule cells are grouped into lamellar clusters, each containing one inhibitory basket cell alongside its excitatory granule cells. Whether a granule cell fires is determined by competition between its external excitatory and inhibitory drive, summarised by the time-averaged ratio of external excitatory to inhibitory conductance (R*_E-I). Granule cells become active when R*_E-I exceeds a threshold R*_th, and the firing rates of the active cells are strongly correlated with R*_E-I. Feedback inhibition from the cluster's basket cell selects the winners: cells above threshold survive and become winners, all others fall silent. This yields the ~5% granule-cell activation degree that is thought to underpin pattern separation.
mapping.ree_translation: This supplies the H3 leg with an operator specification rather than an analogy. The SD-016 tagger currently produces 16 slot logits and softmaxes them, which has no mechanism by which one slot's drive suppresses another's -- and the empirical result is that it sits at the uniform saddle. The Kim & Lim skeleton is: (1) compute each slot's drive, (2) compute a shared inhibitory quantity pooled over the competing set, (3) let each slot survive or not according to its drive RELATIVE to that pool, against a threshold, (4) renormalise over survivors only. That is implementable as a k-WTA / thresholded lateral-inhibition layer inside extract_cue_context, and it is the concrete form of the 'minimal selection-mode knob' the portfolio scope recommends for H3. It also supplies the diagnostic prediction: if the operator is doing its job, the surviving-slot count should be small and STABLE while WHICH slots survive varies with context -- which is exactly the C1 (entropy) plus C1b (context-divergence) pair SD-016 already instruments, and it predicts they should move together rather than independently.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a spiking biophysical model, and essentially none of its machinery transfers literally: conductance ratios time-averaged over a spiking simulation have no counterpart in a single-tick feedforward tagger, and the lamellar-cluster organisation (one basket cell per local cluster) is a topological structure SD-016's flat 16-slot array does not have. Importing it as a single global inhibition term is a substantive change to the modelled architecture, not a faithful reduction. Further, the model ASSUMES the WTA framing it explains -- it is evidence about the dynamics that produce sparse selection given a DG-like circuit, and cannot be cited as independent evidence that the dentate gyrus performs pattern separation (the Espinoza 2018 and Neunuebel 2014 entries carry that). Finally, the ~5% activation regime does not scale to 16 slots, so the model cannot tell us what k should be.
mapping.source_context: Computational/simulation study; conductance-based spiking network model of rat dentate gyrus incorporating entorhinal input, HIPP-cell-mediated feedforward inhibition, mossy-cell excitation and basket-cell feedback inhibition. No new empirical data.

confidence_components.notes: Physical Review E is a reputable venue for computational neuroscience but this is a single-group modelling paper with no empirical component and modest citation impact; source_quality set accordingly at 0.62. Mapping fidelity 0.70 -- the algorithmic skeleton (relative drive against a pooled inhibitory signal, thresholded) transfers cleanly and is the reason to include the paper at all, but the lamellar-cluster topology and the spiking time axis do not. Transfer risk 0.45 is the highest in this pull: a biophysical spiking model is several abstraction levels away from a feedforward tagger, and the ~5% sparsity regime does not instantiate at 16 slots. Aggregate 0.66 weights mapping_fidelity per the skill's guidance for architectural claims, but is capped by the fact that this is modelling rather than measurement.
